run.topic: make my Claude Code sub-agents (and sessions) more token-efficient
run.stack_context: Claude Code power user; also runs Modelproof (informed model selection)
coverage_notes: This run dogfoods Skillproof: it researches how to make sub-agents token-efficient — which is exactly Skillproof's own architecture.
All 8 sources are official Anthropic / Claude Code docs. Three practitioner blogs (hackernoon, amitkoth, richsnapp) were egress-blocked (403) and excluded rather than guessed.
YouTube 0 — local backend IP-blocked from this cloud container (documented caveat). A residential run adds creator-video findings with timestamps.
2 claims were corroborated by ≥2 independent official pages (delegate-verbose-to-subagent; route-mechanical-subagents-to-haiku) — confidence held at high with both sources cited.

findings.claim: Give every mechanical sub-agent (search, extract, format, dedup, fetch-and-distill) a `model: haiku` line in its frontmatter — the `model` field defaults to `inherit` (your expensive main-session model) if omitted, and Claude Code lists cost control via cheaper models as an explicit sub-agent purpose.

source.title: Create custom subagents — Claude Code Docs
source.author: Anthropic

findings.evidence_quote: by routing tasks to faster, cheaper models like Haiku

corroborating_sources.title: Manage costs effectively — Claude Code Docs
corroborating_sources.quote: For simple subagent tasks, specify `model: haiku`

payload.change: add `model: haiku` to the frontmatter of mechanical sub-agents
payload.note: Corroborated by the sub-agents and costs docs.

findings.claim: Shadow the built-in Explore agent with your own `~/.claude/agents/Explore.md` that sets `model: haiku`, so codebase search/exploration stops piggybacking on whatever pricey model your main session runs (Explore just inherits it, capped at Opus).

source.author: Anthropic

findings.claim: For an MCP server only one sub-agent needs (a Playwright or a heavy DB server), define it inline in that sub-agent's `mcpServers` frontmatter instead of `.mcp.json`, so its tool descriptions never load into — or tax — your main conversation's context.

source.title: Create custom subagents — Claude Code Docs
source.author: Anthropic

findings.evidence_quote: define it inline here rather than in `.mcp.json`. The subagent gets the tools; the parent conversation doesn't.

payload.change: add an `mcpServers:` block to the sub-agent frontmatter instead of the global .mcp.json

findings.claim: For your own interactive sessions, run the `opusplan` model setting: it uses Opus during plan mode and auto-switches to Sonnet for execution, so you pay Opus rates only for reasoning-heavy planning, not the bulk implementation tokens.
findings.evidence_quote: Special mode that uses `opus` during plan mode, then switches to `sonnet` for execution

payload.note: Or set it in settings for a standing default.

findings.claim: Move workflow-specific instructions (PR-review steps, migration playbooks, deploy rules) out of CLAUDE.md into on-demand skills, and keep each CLAUDE.md under 200 lines — everything in CLAUDE.md loads into context every session even when irrelevant to the task.

source.title: Manage costs effectively — Claude Code Docs
source.author: Anthropic

findings.evidence_quote: moving specialized instructions into skills keeps your base context smaller. Aim to keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines by including only essentials.

payload.command: move per-workflow rules → ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md; trim CLAUDE.md to essentials

findings.claim: Trim connected MCP servers — run `/mcp` and disable any you're not actively using, prefer CLI tools (like `gh`) over MCP where possible, and run `/context` to see exactly what's consuming your window before real work.

source.title: Manage costs effectively — Claude Code Docs
source.author: Anthropic

findings.evidence_quote: Run `/mcp` to see configured servers and disable any you're not actively using.

findings.claim: Delegate verbose or research-heavy work (reading many files, running tests, fetching docs) to a sub-agent so the bulky output stays in the sub-agent's separate context and only a short summary returns — the single biggest lever for keeping your main context clean.

findings.evidence_quote: the verbose output stays in the subagent's context while only the relevant summary returns to your main conversation.

+ - Delegate verbose/research-heavy work (many file reads, test runs, doc fetches) to a sub-agent;

findings.claim: Always tell a sub-agent exactly what compact output to return (e.g. "report only the failing tests with their error messages") — its full result is pasted back into your main conversation, so several sub-agents each returning walls of text bloat context as badly as not delegating.

source.title: Create custom subagents — Claude Code Docs
source.author: Anthropic

findings.evidence_quote: Running many subagents that each return detailed results can consume significant context.

payload.diff: + - Every sub-agent prompt must specify the compact output to return; never let it dump raw walls of text back.

findings.claim: Don't spawn a sub-agent for a quick single-fact lookup or a small targeted edit — a sub-agent starts with a fresh, empty context and adds latency, so for anything fast just do it inline.

source.title: Create custom subagents — Claude Code Docs
source.author: Anthropic

findings.evidence_quote: Latency matters. Subagents start fresh and may need time to gather context

payload.diff: + - Don't delegate quick single-fact lookups or small edits — sub-agents start empty + add latency; do those inline.

findings.claim: Remember parallel fan-out isn't free: every concurrent agent keeps its own context window, so running many at once multiplies spend (agent teams burn ~7× a normal session). On a tight budget, run explorations sequentially and keep any parallel batch small.

source.title: Manage costs effectively — Claude Code Docs
source.author: Anthropic

findings.evidence_quote: Agent teams use approximately 7x more tokens than standard sessions when teammates run in plan mode, because each teammate maintains its own context window

payload.diff: + - Parallel fan-out multiplies tokens (each agent has its own window; agent teams ≈ 7×). Keep batches small on a tight budget.

findings.claim: Make this your standing routing default: Haiku for simple/mechanical tasks, Sonnet for most day-to-day work, Opus only for the hardest synthesis/reasoning. Never burn Opus on mechanical sub-agent work.
findings.evidence_quote: Choose Haiku for simple tasks, Sonnet for most production workloads, and Opus for the most complex reasoning

payload.diff: + - Routing default: Haiku = simple/mechanical, Sonnet = most work, Opus = hardest synthesis only. Never Opus on grunt work.

findings.claim: Before reaching for a bigger model, tune the effort level instead — Anthropic says effort is often the better lever. Add `effort:` to sub-agent frontmatter: `low`/`medium` for cheap mechanical workers, `xhigh` for hard coding/agentic work.

source.title: Choosing the right model — Claude Platform Docs
source.author: Anthropic

findings.evidence_quote: Tuning effort is often a better lever than switching models.

payload.diff: + - Before switching to a bigger model, tune effort (low/medium mechanical, xhigh hard work) — often the better lever.

findings.claim: Anchor Modelproof's routing math to the real gap: Haiku 4.5 is $1/$5 per MTok (in/out) vs Opus 4.8 at $5/$25 — a flat 5× on both — so moving high-volume mechanical sub-agent work off Opus cuts that slice of spend by ~80%.
findings.evidence_quote: Using Claude Haiku 4.5 at $1/MTok input, $5/MTok output

payload.diff: + - Price anchor: Haiku 4.5 $1/$5 vs Opus 4.8 $5/$25 per MTok (5×). Mechanical volume off Opus ≈ 80% cheaper for that slice.

findings.claim: Prune CLAUDE.md ruthlessly: for each line ask "would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes?" and cut it if not. Bloat isn't just wasted tokens — an over-long CLAUDE.md makes Claude ignore your real instructions because they get buried.

source.title: Best practices for Claude Code — Claude Code Docs
source.author: Anthropic

findings.evidence_quote: If not, cut it. Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!

payload.diff: + - Prune CLAUDE.md per line: "would removing this cause a mistake?" If not, cut it — bloat buries the real rules.

findings.claim: Before starting a long new task mid-session, run `/compact` with a focus (e.g. `/compact focus on the auth bug fix`) instead of waiting for auto-compaction to guess what to keep; add a standing compact directive to CLAUDE.md for priorities you always want preserved.

source.title: Explore the context window — Claude Code Docs
source.author: Anthropic

findings.evidence_quote: run `/compact` with instructions, like `/compact focus on the auth bug fix`, before starting a long new task.

payload.diff: + - Before a long new task mid-session, `/compact` with a focus rather than waiting for auto-compaction.

findings.claim: Lean on prompt caching (automatic; cache reads ≈ a tenth of fresh-input cost) but don't invalidate the cached prefix mid-session — changing tool definitions (e.g. connecting/disconnecting an MCP server) wipes the entire cache. Keep your MCP/tool set stable within a session.
findings.evidence_quote: Modifying tool definitions (names, descriptions, parameters) invalidates the entire cache

payload.diff: + - Keep the MCP/tool set stable within a session — changing tool definitions invalidates the whole prompt cache.
